Write the processing report of a detection set

Source: R/processing_report.R
processing_report.Rd

Writes one self-contained HTML file that records what happened to a detection set: what came in, every logged step with its counts before and after, the data-entry checks, receiver listening, the detections removed by reason, the mortality bands and calls, up to six figures, and the R session. The sections and their order are the same in every report. Every number is read from the processing log (detset_log()) or from the tables of the detection set, never typed. A section whose step did not run says so.

Usage

processing_report(
  x,
  file,
  figures = c("attrition", "abacus", "receivers", "timeline"),
  bands = NULL,
  sections = getOption("detqc.report_sections", list()),
  control = list()
)

Arguments

x

A detset.

file

Path of the HTML file to write. Its folder must exist.

figures

Up to six figures: names of built-in figures, or functions; see Figures. NULL or an empty vector draws none.

bands

Optional result of detect_mortality(), shown as the mortality bands. When x carries review cards from build_mortality_cards() or review_mortality(), the mortality section links to their index.

sections

Named list of functions that add sections; see Adding a section.

control

A list of options, as build_mortality_cards() takes: title, the title of the report (default "Detection processing report"), and outline, an sf polygon of the water body in WGS 84, drawn under the stations of the receivers map.

Value

The path of the file, invisibly.

Details

The report also checks the log. Each record must start where the one before it ended, lose no detection it does not count as removed, and add detections only if it is a load step. The summary flags every record that breaks one of these rules, and any change to the detections after the last record.

The file holds its styles and figures inline (PNG images in base64) and loads nothing from outside, so it opens offline and can be sent by email. No pandoc or R Markdown is needed.

Figures. figures names up to six figures. The built-in ones are "attrition" (detections left after each logged step, drawn from the log), "abacus" (detections over time per animal, from plot_abacus()), "receivers" (stations and their detections, from plot_receivers()) and "timeline" (deployments over time, from plot_timeline()). The receivers map is fitted to the stations that heard a detection and draws control$outline, the lake, under them; the timeline covers the time of the detections; and each figure is as tall as its rows need. A figure whose plot function is missing or stops is listed as not drawn, with the reason. An element of figures can also be a function of x that returns a ggplot of your own; name it, and give it a caption with attr(f, "caption"). Each figure needs its own name. The report saves every figure with ggplot2::ggsave(), 1,800 px wide at 200 dpi.

Adding a section. sections is a named list of functions. Each takes the detection set and returns a data frame (shown as a table), a character vector (shown as paragraphs), or a list of text and table. The name is the section heading. Added sections come after the figures, marked as added, and their numbers are not traced to the log. To add a section to every report in a session, set options(detqc.report_sections = list(...)).

See also

detset_log()

Examples

study <- detqc_example
dets <- detset(study$detections, study$deployments, study$animals)
report_file <- processing_report(dets, tempfile(fileext = ".html"), figures = NULL)
file.exists(report_file)
#> [1] TRUE

# A section of your own: detections per animal.
per_animal <- function(dets) {
  as.data.frame(table(animal_id = dets$detections$animal_id))
}
processing_report(dets, tempfile(fileext = ".html"), figures = NULL,
                  sections = list("Detections per animal" = per_animal))
